places.name: the Wayside Motel office
places.design: Inside: A small, dated motel office from the late 1970s. Worn, honey-brown wooden counter dominates, fronted by peeling laminate. A single, swing-arm brass desk lamp (old, warm filament bulb, sometimes flickering) casts a low circle of light. Walls are painted a once-eggshell colour, now stained and dull. Telling objects: a worn leather-bound guest book always open on the counter, a brass service bell beside it, an old rotary phone near the wall under a corkboard with faded flyers. A large, grimy window looks out into the night or grey dawn. At night, the only light is the desk lamp; shadows are thick. places.name: the roadside motel exterior
places.design: Outside: A single-story, L-shaped concrete block motel from the 1970s, run-down and stained. A row of twelve identical dark-green doors, each with a tarnished brass number, runs along a cracked concrete walkway. A single yellow security light (cold, buzzing, sometimes flickering) on a pole casts harsh shadows. A buzzing neon 'WAYSIDE MOTEL' sign (teal and amber tubes, one letter dim) stands by the empty two-lane road cutting through flat, foggy terrain. Weather is always night with thick, creeping ground fog that swallows distance. The only lit window is the office; all room doors are dark.
